en.title: Count Balanced Binary Substrings Made of Two Contiguous Blocks
en.description:
Count the contiguous substrings in which the numbers of 0s and 1s are equal and each character forms a single contiguous block. Identical text at different positions is counted separately.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; supplements to missing source bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: One line containing a binary string of only 0 and 1. The original upper bound on the length is 100000, and no lower bound is given; this site keeps the empty string (an empty line) as valid.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 4; 6; 0. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Split the string into runs of identical characters; each pair of adjacent runs contributes the smaller of their lengths; sum this over all adjacent pairs.
